answer_raw:
The top cities for quality of life depend entirely on which index you use, with **Copenhagen**, **Canberra**, and **New York** all claiming top spots depending on the specific metric and methodology.

The **EIU Global Liveability Index 2026** ranks **Copenhagen** (Denmark) as the world's most liveable city, followed by **Vienna** (Austria) and **Melbourne** (Australia) [2]. This index assesses 173 cities based on stability, healthcare, culture, environment, education, and infrastructure [1].

The **Oxford Economics 2026 Global Cities Index** offers a different perspective. In its ranking of 1,000 cities, **Canberra** is the top-ranked city for quality of life [5][8]. It is followed by **Bergen** (Norway) and **Singapore** [8]. This specific category measures factors like income equality, life expectancy, crime, and access to recreation [4]. While **Canberra** excels in these metrics, it ranks 45th in the overall index [4]. Conversely, in the overall Global Cities Index, **New York** holds the No. 1 spot, though the US as a whole struggles in the specific quality of life category [3]. The highest-ranked US city for quality of life in this index is **San Jose**, sitting at 13th [5].
